plan: Given my value of $31, I should aim to bid slightly below it to maximize potential profit while minimizing the risk of overpaying. Since there is no past history to consider, I'll assume rational bidding from others. A bid slightly above the midpoint of $31, such as $25, could deter others from bidding too close to their values while still offering a decent profit margin if I win. This strategy balances potential earnings with the likelihood of winning.

Given my private value of $22, I should aim to win the prize while paying less than my value to ensure profit. Since bids can be in $0.1 increments and the other bidders are rational, they might bid close to their values. To maximize profit, I will bid slightly above half of my value to increase my chances of winning while minimizing cost. Thus, I will bid $11.5 to balance the probability of winning with a reasonable payment, maximizing long-term profit.

Given my value of $40, I aim to bid just below this to maximize profit while still having a chance to win. Bidding slightly below my value, say $39.9, allows me to win against slightly lower bids and ensures I pay less than my value if I win. This strategy balances the risk of losing with the potential profit from winning. Since this is the only round, I will not consider past rounds.
